office_does: The three county commissioners are Mason County's legislative body: they adopt the budget, pass ordinances and oversee roads, property and county services. Commissioners are nominated by district and elected county-wide.
race_blurb: Open seat: Commissioner Sharon Trask did not run and resigned in September. Two Shelton City Council members who split on a 2024 homeless-housing sales tax meet again after a five-vote council race in 2021. Democrat Miguel Gutierrez campaigns on housing, health care and living wages; Republican George Blush on cracking down on encampments and blight and ending wasteful spending.

candidates.summary: Shelton City Council member since 2022 and former special education teacher, campaigning on 'Housing, Healthcare, and Hope' for Mason County.
highlights: Calls for living wages, child care, elder care, affordable housing and security from medical bankruptcy [S1]
Voted for a 0.1% city sales tax to house people who are homeless and fund their services, rejected 4-3 [S9]
Voted to give the downtown homeless shelter's operator $20,000 and sits on its board [S1][S10]
Moved to pause the city's Flock license-plate camera contract [S12]
Endorsed by former county auditors and commissioners and by the Mason County Democrats [S5]

housing.basis: Voted for a city sales tax to house people who are homeless and lists affordable housing among his goals: public investment in housing.

taxes.basis: Voted for a new 0.1% city sales tax (about $310,000 a year) for homeless housing and services.

spending.basis: Platform of new public programs (living wages, child care, elder care, security from medical bankruptcy) delivered through government.

safety.basis: Backed homeless shelter funding and a homeless-services tax, and moved to pause the city's license-plate camera contract; no stated policing platform.

experience.basis: Second-term city council member (elected 2021, re-elected 2025) with an elected record, though new to county office.

candidates.summary: Shelton City Council member, park board president and Mason County Housing Authority chair who runs a downtown restaurant, campaigning for a 'cleaner, safer, and more prosperous' county.
highlights: Would unite code enforcement with the Sheriff's Office against illegal dumping, encampments and blight [S1]
Promises to end wasteful spending and live within the county's means [S1]
Voted against a 0.1% city sales tax for homeless housing and services [S6]
Would restore animal control and expand water access for wildfire fighting [S1]
Endorsed by the Mason County Republican Party; first of the party's three nominees for the vacant seat [S1][S8]

safety.basis: Enforcement-first platform: code enforcement working with the sheriff against encampments, dumping and blight, and 'cracking down on crime and encampments.'

spending.basis: Explicit commitment to 'ending wasteful spending and living within our means' and fiscal responsibility.

taxes.basis: Voted against a new 0.1% city sales tax for homeless housing and services.

experience.basis: Runs on 'proven government, business, and nonprofit leadership experience': city council since 2024, park board president and housing authority chair.
